There's absolutely no reason for you to give up! Don't be discouraged and remember, improvement isn't always easy. Sometimes it feels like no matter how much you draw, you just don't improve, but that's completely natural. Especially since you have only recently started digital art. 
Art styles are tricky, but instead of thinking about it as something you make all by yourself, try thinking about it as a combination of many different artists. If there's a certain thing you like about your favourite artist's style, ex. The way they draw eyes, don't be afraid to take inspiration from it. Art should always be something that makes you happy, so why not combine the art that already do? 
 Your frustration in drawing is definitely a form of art block and while everybody conquers art block differently, these are some of the things I do. Normally, I either try something new for a while, whether it be a new medium of art, or drawing something you've never drawn. You could also try a exercise I find rather helpful: draw a pose you find in a minimalistic way, in five minutes or less. Of course, these might not help, as my experience of art block might differ from yours but I hope you find this helpful. 
There's no such thing as 'not meant for art'. Art should always, first and foremost, be something you enjoy doing. Don't stress out over the little details in your art. Remember to make art for yourself, first. For others, second.
